source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.
source.original_treatment_name: Lindera benzoin (L.) Blume var. pubescens (E.J. Palmer & Steyerm.) Rehder

morphology_documented.habit: Dioecious or polygamo-dioecious much-branched shrub or small tree to ca. 5 m
morphology_documented.twigs: Young branches pubescent, brownish; flowers precede foliage (genus key)
morphology_documented.leaves: Aromatic entire obovate, elliptic or ovate blades (4–)6–15 × 2–6 cm, tapering or cuneate basally, pubescent and glaucous beneath; petioles ca. 10 mm
morphology_documented.flowers: Nearly sessile clusters at nodes along branchlets or tips; fragrant; 6 yellow sepals; pistillate flowers have ca. 12–18 reduced stamens
morphology_documented.fruit: Red drupe 6–10 × 3–7 mm on 3–5 mm pedicel

source_scope_note: Genus and key details explicitly noted; where historical flora lacks a species treatment, morphology is limited to independently named secondary sources.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Historical treatment specifically var. pubescens, not necessarily whole species concept
Flora Lauraceae key contrasts unlobed pinnately veined Lindera leaves with often-lobed Sassafras
preservation: Additive, original taxon records, photos, attribution and site unchanged
